study.title: Proverbs 15 - words that heal, a heart that is subject and fear that leads to wisdom
study.overview: Proverbs 15 brings together short sayings that contrast the just and the perverse, especially in the use of speech, in the disposition of the heart and in the response to correction. The chapter shows that mild words, wise counsel, humility and fear of the LORD produce life, peace and understanding; arrogance, verbal violence, stubbornness and greed spread conflict and lead to ruin. The text also insists that God sees, weighs and responds to human paths, accepting the prayer of the righteous and rejecting pride and wickedness.

outline.title: The speech that scifica or destroys
outline.explanation: The first proverbs deal with the tongue: the soft response calms the anger, the speech of the wise communicates knowledge, and the whole language is like a tree of life; in contrast, the perverse word hurts and breaks the spirit.

outline.title: Correction, reverence and the gaze of God
outline.explanation: Here the discipline received in the family, the difference between the sacrifice of the wicked and the prayer of the righteous, the aversion of God to the ungodly way and his full perception of human hearts, even of death and perdition.

outline.title: Humility before the rebuke and fruit of the heart
outline.explanation: The mockery rejects correction, while the wise man welcomes her. The text connects joy, prudence, fear of the LORD and dominion of wrath to a more peaceful life; it also contrasts the lazy with the diligent and teaches that contentment is worth more than the abundance without peace.

outline.title: Council, timely words and the path of humility
outline.explanation: The final section values the wise son, the plural counsel, the well thought out response and the prayer of the righteous. The chapter ends by teaching that fear of the Lord instructs wisdom and that humility precedes honor.

study.context: The chapter belongs to the sapiential literature of Proverbs, whose form is that of short sentences that instruct daily life. The content itself shows a family and community environment in which parents, children, wise, scoffers, just and perverse coexist, with speech, discipline and inner posture central themes. The notes provided also highlight the practical importance of speaking with mildness, accepting correction and depending on fear of the Lord.
study.theology: Theologically, Proverbs 15 presents God as sovereign and attentive: his eyes reach all, his judgment weighs ways and thoughts, and his closeness is given to the righteous in response to prayer. The chapter teaches that wisdom is not mere verbal ability, but a life shaped by reverence to God, humility, and willingness to be corrected. The fear of the LORD is not empty dread; he corrects self-sufficient, dementing the illusion of independence and guides wise choices. There is also a strong relational ethics: peace is preserved by meekness, the house is shaken by greed, and honor is prepared by humility. In Protestant evangelical reading, this points to the need for a transformed heart, because the problem is not only the external discourse, but the interior that produces it.

scholarViews.insight: The fear of the LORD favors humility, because the due respect for God corrects the illusion of self-reliance.
The mild response can disperse anger and preserve peace, while rough words tend to worsen it.
The wise language requires discernment to know when to speak, what to say and how to say, according to the occasion.

questions: In what situations do my words tend to increase tension rather than produce peace?
Have I received correction as a path to wisdom or as a personal offense?
How can the fear of the LORD deliver me from self-reliance and become humbler?
study.practice: This week, practice three attitudes of the chapter: respond with mildness in a difficult conversation, accept a reproof without defending himself immediately and ask God to use his holy fear to correct his motivations. Also choose a timely word of encouragement or advice for someone from your home or church, thinking less about winning the discussion and more in building the person.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided are only excerpts, so some statements of the commentators appear summarized and do not cover the whole chapter. There is no basis for notes for broader historical details, dates, specific authorship or geographic reconstructions; therefore, the study avoids these conclusions. Where the text speaks of death, Xelol and perdition, language is treated according to the proverb itself and not as a technical explanation of a complete system of life after death.
